609:     // A cap that folds over a box edge (crossings on two faces of the shell)
610:     // is not planar. Its pieces would have to be built on the surface, not on
611:     // the mean plane, or the cell stops closing — so it stays ONE face, and
612:     // the region is the one covering most of its projected area, which is
613:     // what the pieces below are used for in that case.
614:     //
615:     // A vertex the carve took as ON the surface is within its ON band of
616:     // it, not on it, so a flat cap holding one is off its mean plane by up
617:     // to that band — and is still flat. Tri_angle (2026-09-23): a grid
618:     // corner 0.29 mm off Rack_1's outlet plane (the band is 0.32 mm) made
619:     // the bottom-row cap read as folded, it was not split at the outlet_p0 /
620:     // outlet_wall boundary, and the wall took a 12.8 mm strip of the fan
621:     // opening.
622:     const scalar hloop = std::sqrt(area);
623:     const bool planar = offPlane <= std::max(scalar(1e-3) * hloop, onTol);

1379:     // ---- canonicalise near-duplicate surface coordinates -----------------
1380:     // An STL written from float32 geometry carries ONE physical plane as
1381:     // several coordinates: Shinaide's rack side arrives as both 1.490737 and
1382:     // 1.490738, and its containment baffle -- coplanar with that rack side --
1383:     // as 1.490738. Cutting against the pair leaves a 1 um sliver between two
1384:     // copies of the same wall: 8 open cells, aspect ratio 3.6e4 and 22 skewed
1385:     // faces on that case alone, all of them clustered on those planes.
1386:     // Snapping the vertices makes the plane single-valued, so the two cuts
1387:     // coincide exactly and no sliver is ever created.
1388:     //
1389:     // FDS does this by default (SNAP_GEOM_NODES, geom.f90:15662) and rewrites
1390:     // surface nodes onto the cutting plane's analytic value at
1391:     // SNAP_DIST_FACTOR = 1e-4*dx (geom.f90:5348); the same fraction of the
1392:     // finest cell is used here. Deterministic and rank-independent: the
1393:     // clusters come from the surface coordinates alone.
1394:     if (backgroundSpacing > 0 && maxLevel_ >= 0)
1395:     {
1396:         const scalar finest =
1397:             backgroundSpacing / scalar(label(1) << maxLevel_);
1398:         // Grid planes first, then the export-quantisation clusters: a value
1399:         // already on a plane is at least `finest` from every other plane, so
1400:         // the (100x tighter) cluster pass can never pull it back off.
1401:         if (grid && gridSnapFraction > 0)
1402:         {
1403:             snapToGridPlanes(*grid, gridSnapFraction * finest);
1404:         }
1405:         if (coordSnapFraction > 0)
1406:         {
1407:             snapSurfaceCoordinates(coordSnapFraction * finest);
1408:         }
1409:     }

1425:     // ---- near-coincidence weld (DAML thin-wall wedge WP, route 1) --------
1426:     // Runs AFTER both snaps and BEFORE any point-derived data (shells, baffle
1427:     // sheets, cached trees): coordinates are canonical by now, so the weld's
1428:     // exact-position vertex classes are the same on every rank, and a value
1429:     // the 0.01-scale grid snap already put on a plane is exactly 0 from it
1430:     // and outside the weld's (1e-6, weldTol] band. See weldNearCoincident.
1431:     if (grid && weldTolerance > 0)
1432:     {
1433:         weldNearCoincident
1434:         (
1435:             *grid, weldTolerance, weldRounds,
1436:             firstLayerMinFraction, firstLayerMax, firstLayerSealGap
1437:         );
1438:     }
